body_ar: "الثانية تفسير التولة" وهي ما كانوا يزعمون أنه يحبب الرجل إلى امرأته أو المرأة إلى زوجها، ومثلها كل ما كان كذلك كما يتخذ من الخرز الذي يحبب الإنسان إلى الناس كما يزعمون وهو أيضا فيه ضرب من السحر لأنه في كثير من الأحيان يتخذ لابتزاز الناس وأخذ أموالهم، "الثالثة أن هذه الثلاث كلها من الشرك من غير استثناء" قوله من غير استثناء قد سبق الاستثناء وصرح به هو في قوله: وخص منها الدليل ما خلا من الشرك، فالمقصود منها ما كان من الشرك فهو منهي عنه من غير استثناء،
body_en: 'Second: the explanation of al-tiwalah' — it is what they used to claim makes a man beloved to his wife, or a woman beloved to her husband. Like it is everything of that sort, such as the beads that are taken up to make a person beloved to people, as they claim; and there is in it too a kind of sorcery, because in many cases it is taken up in order to extort from people and take their wealth. 'Third: that these three are all of them a form of associating partners with God (shirk), without exception.' As for his words 'without exception': the exception has already been made, and he himself stated it plainly when he said, 'and the evidence has singled out from among them whatever is free of shirk.' So what is meant is: whatever among them involves shirk is subject to the prohibition (manhī ʿanhu), without exception,

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.arabic: فهو منهي عنه من غير استثناء
flags.context: فالمقصود منها ما كان من الشرك فهو منهي عنه من غير استثناء
options: is subject to the prohibition (manhī ʿanhu)
flags.note: The Sheikh says manhī ʿanhu ('subject to a prohibition'), not ḥarām. In uṣūl the two are not automatically equivalent — a prohibition may be read as producing karāhah rather than taḥrīm — and he does not here take the further step of naming the ruling. Rendering it 'forbidden (ḥarām)' would put a ruling word in his mouth. Kept at the level he used it.

flags.context: "الثانية تفسير التولة" وهي ما كانوا يزعمون أنه يحبب الرجل إلى امرأته
options: al-tiwalah, a charm for winning a spouse's love
flags.note: The Sheikh supplies his own definition in the next clause, so the term has been transliterated and left for his gloss to carry rather than being pre-translated.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.
The base text quoted here is in verse (naẓm). Per the style guide it is rendered as prose; the Arabic is retained in the bilingual pane.
وخص منها الدليل ما خلا من الشرك is a line of the versified base text quoted from memory, not the Sheikh's prose; it has been kept in quotation marks.
'These three' refers to three items enumerated earlier in the chapter, which are not in the written excerpt. The referent cannot be recovered from this page.
